review_notes: I read the whole file. I then compared its main declarations (ker, congr, mapGen, correspondence, lift, kerLift, map, and the isomorphism theorems) with the Con analogues in Mathlib/GroupTheory/Congruence/Hom.lean and Basic.lean. I also compared them with the TwoSidedIdeal kernel and operations files, Ideal.Quotient, and RingQuot. The RingCon declarations are the intended ring-level counterparts of the monoid-level Con API, and they are built on RingCon's own structure and on the Con/AddCon lemmas. They are not independent copies of one concept. TwoSidedIdeal.ker is a different representation, and the file there has a TODO to reuse RingCon.ker, which would be a change in that file, not this one. RingQuot is a different construction. In this file, map/factorₐ and the S/non-S/ₐ variants are named specialisations with their own simp lemmas, so I did not report them as competing duplicates. I found no clear cost from a competing duplicate concept, so I abstain.
